title: A Spire for the Crown Again
premise: Freya Joubert, a beast-speaker who hides her forbidden gift behind the ledgers of the Vellum Guild—a trade house dealing in impossible things—has spent her life being invisible. When the crown declares a hunt for all gifted souls and her own guildmaster sells names to save himself, Freya flees into the wilds where she learns the beasts' unrest stems from a broken covenant between human and animal realms, one her grandmother helped shatter. Hunted by a zealous inquisitor and shadowed by a disgraced knight who owes her his life, Freya must gather three covenant-keys held by factions that hate each other. In the end she reforges the covenant at the Spire—at the cost of her secret identity, revealed to the very court that hunted her—and wins not pardon but a new law: truth spoken openly, loyalty chosen rather than commanded.
about_author: Yara Halloran is a former archivist who writes fantasy about people who keep dangerous records. She lives near a coastal forest where she insists the crows are gossiping about her.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. We meet her balancing the Vellum Guild's strange accounts—bottled storms, borrowed shadows—while secretly soothing a wounded messenger hawk with her gift. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness; she believes invisibility is safety.

chapters.title: A Proclamation Nailed to Every Door
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The crown announces the Gift-Hunt: all beast-speakers to be registered or burned. The guildmaster orders staff to report 'anomalies.' Freya overhears him drafting a list of names. Beat: fear curdling into betrayal as her sanctuary becomes a trap.

chapters.title: What the Rats Knew
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Using rats as informants, she confirms the guildmaster sold fourteen gifted names—including hers—to the inquisitor Serah Vane. She burns her page from the ledger and flees by night. Beat: grief for the life she built, resolve hardening.

chapters.title: The Knight Who Owed Her
chapters.summary: Dain Corvath's POV. A disgraced knight hunting runaways corners Freya in the marshes—but she once saved his horse's life, and the mare refuses to let him raise his sword. He lets her go, then follows anyway. Beat: reluctant alliance born of debt.

chapters.title: Where the Beasts Went Silent
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Deep in the Thornwood, animals flee them in unnatural silence. An old wolf speaks of the Broken Covenant: when the realms' pact shattered, beasts lost their voices to humans and their trust. Beat: awe and guilt—her gift is a fragment of what was lost.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Confession
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In a ruined waystation she finds her grandmother's journal: the Joubert family helped break the covenant generations ago to buy the guild its trading privileges. Beat: identity shaken—the hunted discovers her blood helped cause the hunt.

chapters.title: Serah Vane's Method
chapters.summary: Serah Vane's POV. The inquisitor interrogates the captured guildmaster, revealing she genuinely believes gifts are a plague on justice. Flashback shows why: a beast-speaker's ravens killed her family. Beat: the antagonist gains tragic weight; she is not wrong about everything.

chapters.title: The First Key: Salt and Bone
chapters.summary: Freya and Dain's POV alternating. They bargain with the drowned-folk of Greyharbor for the first covenant-key, paying with Dain's knightly oath spoken aloud and surrendered. Beat: cost made literal; loyalty begins shifting from crown to companion.

chapters.title: A Market of Stolen Names
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At an underground market for the hidden gifted, Freya finds other speakers living in terror—and a child whose gift mirrors her own. She promises protection she may not be able to give. Beat: responsibility; invisibility now feels like cowardice.

chapters.title: Vane Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Vane raids the market; the child is taken, Freya barely escapes with the second key won in the chaos. Dain is recognized and arrested covering her retreat. Beat: devastating loss; the hunt turns personal.

chapters.title: The Prisoner's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. In the crown dungeon, Dain negotiates with Vane: he'll lead her to Freya if the child goes free. He plans betrayal of both sides. Beat: loyalty vs. truth tearing him apart; he no longer knows which master he serves.

chapters.title: The Mountain That Remembers
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Guided by wolves, she reaches the Spire's roots, where the third key sleeps inside a stone guardian who tests her with her grandmother's crimes. She confesses them aloud. Beat: acceptance—she cannot outrun her inheritance, only redeem it.

chapters.title: Two Traitors at the Treeline
chapters.summary: Freya and Dain's POV. Dain arrives with Vane's soldiers, signals warning too late; Freya is captured. But the child, freed by Dain's bargain, has told the beasts everything. Beat: apparent defeat laced with hope neither sees yet.

chapters.title: Trial by Crown
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the capital, Freya is publicly tried. Offered pardon for naming other speakers, she instead reads her grandmother's confession aloud to the court. Beat: defiance—truth weaponized against the lie the crown is built on.

chapters.title: The Riot of Small Voices
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Every rat, raven, and hound in the city speaks at once, demanding the covenant be heard. Chaos floods the trial; Vane's authority cracks as soldiers' own horses refuse orders. Beat: exhilaration—the silenced find their voice through her.

chapters.title: Serah's Wound Reopened
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Confronted by Freya privately, Vane learns the ravens that killed her family were coerced by a corrupt magistrate—the covenant-breakers, not the gifted. Her certainty fractures. Beat: antagonist's crisis; vengeance loses its target.

chapters.title: Escape on Wings Not Ours
chapters.summary: Freya and Dain's POV. Freed by a flock-led prison break, they race for the Spire with two keys while Vane, half-converted, buys them time with her own badge. Beat: uneasy trust; former hunter now shield.

chapters.title: The Spire Awakens
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the summit, the third key demands a speaker willing to bind herself permanently as the covenant's living anchor—her voice, forever shared with every beast. Beat: terror and clarity; this is what her whole hidden life was preparing her for.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Crown reinforcements arrive; Dain stands alone on the stair against his former brothers-in-arms, refusing to move. Beat: sacrifice without spectacle—he chooses truth over the oath that defined him.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Climax. Freya speaks the covenant anew, her voice joined by wolf, hawk, whale, and the child speaker below. The Spire blazes; the old law dies; every gifted person in the realm feels the bond rekindle. Beat: transcendent, costly triumph.

chapters.title: A New Law, Written Openly
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The crown, humbled before witnesses, ratifies the Speaker's Accord; Vane becomes its first honest enforcer; the guildmaster faces the ledger of his own crimes. Beat: justice achieved outside the old law's machinery.

chapters.title: The Voice That Is Never Alone
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Epilogue. Freya, now the Spire's anchor, keeps new ledgers—not of impossible things traded, but of promises kept between realms. Dain stays; the child visits; the crows gossip kindly. Beat: belonging earned, silence ended, home redefined.
